result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers address every concrete problem and propose similar fixes. B has the stronger save model: settings apply immediately with an Undo toast, failures show next to the setting, and Undo also follows a settings-only reset. B also frames its advice as assumptions rather than measured results, while A claims the engineering ordering is 'almost certainly the main cause', though A's ideas to tally the reviews and add instrumentation are good. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name the same concrete problems and propose similar fixes: default alerts on (or copied from another hive), changes that apply immediately, removing the unit-change popup, grouping the settings, and moving Reset away from Save. A is slightly stronger on how changes are saved and reset, with an Undo toast, failures shown next to the setting, and Undo after a settings-only reset. B gives more ideas for checking after release, but it claims the engineering-order layout is 'almost certainly the main cause' of the reviews, which overstates what it can know without testing.
